content: The SIVA1 gene encodes a protein known as Apoptosis Regulatory Protein Siva, which plays a critical role in the process of programmed cell death (apoptosis) triggered by the CD27 antigen. CD27 is a member of the tumor necrosis factor receptor (TNFR) superfamily. The cytoplasmic tail of the CD27 antigen interacts specifically with the N-terminal region of the Siva protein. Two distinct protein isoforms of Siva, resulting from alternative splicing of the SIVA1 gene, have been identified. The SIVA1 protein has been experimentally shown to interact directly with the CD27 antigen. Siva protein is an intracellular ligand that contains zinc and interacts with the CD4 receptor. It facilitates apoptosis in T-lymphoid cells that is induced by the HIV-1 envelope. Furthermore, recent studies have identified Siva as a direct transcriptional target of the tumor-suppressor proteins p53 and E2F1.
